findings.title: Fallback locales are preloaded only in controller requests, not in jobs or with_locale blocks
findings.body:
The fallback chain is now [locale, site default, :en] for every I18n.t. The accelerated `I18n.translate` loads only `config.locale` (`lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68`), and `load_translations` is overridden to do nothing without explicit filenames, so the backend never lazy-loads a locale on its own. `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is called only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Two other places set the locale without it:
- `app/jobs/base.rb:151` sets `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale` in every job thread.
- `app/services/post_alerter.rb:138` uses `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`.

In both, a key missing from the current locale falls back to `:en`, which may not be loaded in that process. The lookup then returns "translation missing" instead of the English text. A job running with a non-English site locale is the likely case. The result is silent. The fix is to preload the fallback chain wherever the locale is set, for example by making `load_locale` or `translate` load the whole fallback chain. At minimum, call `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` after the locale assignment in `app/jobs/base.rb` and inside the `with_locale` block in `post_alerter.rb`.

findings.title: Ordering comment does not match the file name
findings.body: The comment says "order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb", but the file is named `i18n.rb` with no numeric prefix. Rails loads initializers alphabetically, so it runs after every `NN-` file, including `05-site_settings.rb` (which `FallbackLocaleList` needs for `SiteSetting`) and `99-*`. It works, but only by accident of sorting. The comment suggests a dependency on 02 only. Name the file with a prefix (for example `03-i18n.rb`) or reword the comment to state the real dependencies.

findings.title: Cached translations are not invalidated when the site default locale changes
findings.body: The fallback list depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`. The translate cache in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72` is keyed only by key, `config.locale` and the backend object id. A result that came from a fallback is cached under the user's locale. After an admin changes `default_locale`, cached entries for locales that lack that key can still return the old fallback until they are evicted or `I18n.reload!` runs. I did not find anything that resets the cache on that setting change. Is that acceptable, or should the default_locale change hook call `I18n.reload!`?

findings.title: No specs for the new fallback behaviour
findings.body: The change adds `FallbackLocaleList`, `I18n.ensure_loaded!` and enables fallbacks in all environments. Before, `config.i18n.fallbacks` was set only in production, cloud66 and profile, so test and development never used fallbacks. The PR adds no spec for the fallback order [user, site, en], for loading the fallback locales on demand, or for the `with_locale` and job paths. Add specs for those cases.

contracts.action: Per-request preloading of the fallback locales (I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!)
contracts.equivalent_path: I18n.translate lazy-loads only config.locale via load_locale (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:68); jobs/base.rb:151 and post_alerter.rb:138 set locale without any fallback preload.
contracts.before_after: Before: only the current locale was loaded and there was no fallback. After: the controller also loads the site default locale and :en. Jobs and with_locale blocks still load only the current locale.
contracts.visible_effect: In web requests, missing translations show the site or English text. In jobs and with_locale blocks they may show 'translation missing' if the fallback locale is not already loaded.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent: a missing translation string, with no error raised.

contracts.action: New I18n.ensure_loaded!(locale) in the translate accelerator
contracts.equivalent_path: load_locale, which takes LOAD_MUTEX and re-checks @loaded_locales
contracts.before_after: The new method initialises @loaded_locales outside the mutex and delegates to load_locale, which re-checks inside the mutex. The result is the same as the existing path. The unsynchronised `||=` is not a practical problem.
contracts.failure_mode: If a locale file is missing, load_locale still appends it to @loaded_locales, so it is not retried. This matches the existing behaviour.

summary: Fallbacks are now on in all environments via a custom [user, site, en] list. The fallback locales are preloaded only in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Jobs (`app/jobs/base.rb:151`) and `with_locale` blocks (`app/services/post_alerter.rb:138`) skip that step, so a missing key there can come back as a silent "translation missing". I also flagged a misleading initializer ordering comment, a stale-cache question when `default_locale` changes, and the lack of specs.
